_comment: Encodes .claude/skills/web-stack-advisor/{SKILL.md,references/*.md} as data, so Act 2 (buildTrail.js) and Act 3 (advisorUi.js) render from this file rather than from hardcoded HTML. js/advisor.js's recommendStack() implements the scoring rules this file describes; tests/advisor.test.js checks that pairing against every useCase below.

functionalities.name: Styling and layout
functionalities.meaning: Make it look decent and consistent

functionalities.name: Client interactivity
functionalities.meaning: Filters, tooltips, drill-down without a page reload
functionalities.lightestTool: D3 or vanilla JS; Streamlit/Dash if you want no JS

functionalities.name: API: providing
functionalities.meaning: Expose data or a model over HTTP

functionalities.name: API: consuming
functionalities.meaning: A page or service calls an API

functionalities.name: Server-side compute
functionalities.meaning: Run pandas or a model per request
functionalities.lightestTool: Streamlit/Dash, or any Python web framework

functionalities.name: Persistence
functionalities.lightestTool: SQLite via Django ORM or SQLAlchemy

functionalities.name: Authorization
functionalities.meaning: What may they do or see?

functionalities.name: Background and long jobs
functionalities.meaning: Work that outlives one HTTP request

rungs.name: Static HTML + D3 (+ Tailwind)
rungs.description: Show a finished result. No server.

rungs.name: Streamlit or Dash
rungs.description: Explore data, or a tool for peers. Python only, no JS.

rungs.name: Flask or FastAPI
rungs.description: Serve a model or data over HTTP.

rungs.name: Django (+ Tailwind kit)
rungs.description: Users, database, forms, admin. A multi-user prototype.

rungs.name: React (or Angular) + Tailwind over an API
rungs.description: Only when the UI is genuinely app-like (instant updates, keyboard-driven, complex client state).

useCases.label: Share a chart with teammates
useCases.why: No server to run; the data ships as JSON/CSV.

useCases.label: Explore a dataset
useCases.displayStack: Streamlit first; D3 only for custom visuals
useCases.why: Fastest path from a DataFrame to widgets.

useCases.label: Metrics dashboard for peers
useCases.why: More layout and callback control than Streamlit. (Functionality 9, authentication, is sometimes also needed here - marked "maybe" in the source table - but is not required to reach this pick, so it is left off this use case's needs.)

useCases.label: Demo a model
useCases.displayStack: FastAPI, plus a Streamlit page if a UI is wanted

useCases.label: Labeling or review tool
useCases.why: Forms, auth, admin and ownership filtering are solved.

useCases.label: Multi-user product prototype (default UI)
useCases.why: One project vs two - only pay for a second project when the UI is genuinely app-like.

useCases.label: Multi-user product prototype (app-like UI)
useCases.why: Same functionality set as the default-UI case above - only the app-like-UI flag differs, which is exactly what use-cases.md's "When to escalate a rung" describes for Django to React+API.

useCases.label: Pipeline that ends in a page
useCases.displayStack: Python writes JSON, static D3 renders it
useCases.why: Nothing live to keep running. (The source use case also lists an upstream "data stages" need, which is a Python pipeline step outside the 12 web functionalities, so it does not appear in this needs list.)

audienceTable.label: Business users, read-only
audienceTable.leanToward: Static D3 or Dash, polished with a Tailwind kit

audienceTable.label: Business users, interactive with accounts
audienceTable.leanToward: Django + Tailwind kit, or React + shadcn/ui

escalations.trigger: You need accounts with different data visibility, saved records, or a back-office screen.
You are re-implementing auth, an ORM layer and an admin.

The UI needs instant, app-like interaction, or other systems also need the API, or a front-end engineer will own the UI. Django can grow into this later by adding Django REST Framework; the data model survives.

cautions: Authorization must be enforced on the server. Hiding a button in React is not security.

FastAPI and Tailwind were verified by building and running them (demos/labeling-fastapi-react/, demos/labeling-django/ - in the skill's source repo, not this project). Streamlit and Dash were written from documentation and general knowledge only.
This skill is self-contained and ships no code - a demos/... path it cites is evidence a claim was tested in the skill's source repo, not a folder present wherever the skill is installed.

RQ needs os.fork (no native Windows; WSL required). Celery has dropped Windows support (the solo pool is a dev-only workaround). Huey can use SQLite storage - the verified local default (demos/long-jobs/).
